column1: # compile-pass rows (area compile-pass) for rust-v0.167.0: fixes made by the compile pass (PF-85-S02/S04) in files other slices resolved, plus what it leaves open; kept in their own file to stay clear of the 512,000-byte blob limit; same columns

column17: compile pass: `codex_history::RolloutItem` imported for main's #1129 history readers (latest_runtime_from_model_context, recorded_account_from_model_context); the parent's cache-key policy is read through upstream's `model_client()` accessor (ArcSwap)
compile pass: prompt cache key read through upstream's `model_client()` accessor

compile pass: main's durable-spawn fences (prepare_durable_thread_spawn_parent / persist_durable_thread_spawn) pass `PersistContext::Standard` to upstream's `try_ensure_rollout_materialized(context)`; Standard makes the thread and queued items durable, as main's call did and as upstream's legacy spawn path does
compile pass: main's `RolloutItem::SourceOrigin` (PF-30-S02 origin records) joins the no-op arm of upstream's MCP-runtime replay loop at session start; origins are restored elsewhere

compile pass: main's Refused end event (43bfa16dee) uses upstream's four-field ExecCommandResult (aggregated_output carries the refusal text); main's #442/#826 explain_protected_read now matches upstream's `UnifiedExec` emitter instead of the removed `Shell` one (compile only, see the open row)

compile pass found: `ToolEmitter::finish` (which adds main's #442 protected-read and #826 user-namespace explanations) is called only by apply_patch on the sync branch; unified exec ends commands without it, so neither explanation reaches the person or model for a denied command. S3b must wire it into unified exec's end path (main had it on the shell handler). Explanation only; no permission decision depends on it

compile pass: main's #1701 own-agent check goes through `local_or_unsupported()` (upstream's AgentControl trait object); any other backend treats every target as foreign (fail closed), as multi_agents_common::ensure_own_agent does

compile pass: PF-84-S03's level-in-force check reads the policy through `local_or_unsupported()`; another backend or an unreadable policy counts as Aggressive (fail closed, as before); the approval-off test uses upstream's `TurnContext::approval_policy()`
